prospect.name: Marian G. Samson
prospect.occupation: Runs his own company — 'I make deals all, all, all day'; mostly seated or driving; recently moved house
prospect.family_status: Two daughters, one 12 and one almost six; providing for his family
prospect.training_background: Largely untrained. Bought 10 kg and 16 kg kettlebells about two weeks ago and started following Trevor's videos, having watched them for two to three months. Trained heavily in a gym last year while using anabolic steroids and stopped. Was a good runner as a teenager until the knee injury and has not run since. History of repeated starts and stops — 'I tried and I give up. And I tried and I give up.'
prospect.medical: Disc compression in the lower back with a curved posture, diagnosed about three years ago. Elevated blood pressure for two years, untreated. Right knee unstable since an untreated injury roughly ten years ago. Left hip locked with markedly reduced mobility, which he says has disturbed his gait — 'my walking is also, it's like disturbed about this because of these issues.' New back pain reported on the prior call after starting kettlebells himself. Prior anabolic steroid use, stopped. High work stress, about six hours of sleep.

signals: Explicitly wants a former self back and dates it: 'The version of you from about 14 years ago' — his own target is the 90 kg he last was at around 1995 by his reckoning
Names the ground he has lost: 'I didn't run since I got my knee injury... I can remember how fast I was when I was running and I was jumping'

Carries the regret openly — 'I'm looking in the mirror and I say, okay, what the , I should do something' and 'I think I'm heading downwards in this game at this point. And I will be more and more weak'
A history of restarts rather than a first attempt: 'it will be like Monday, and Monday, and Monday. And this Monday never comes'
Not the preserver type despite the medical stack — he is chasing recovery of capability, not maintenance of it

goals.text: Get back to 90 kg from 105 kg and look good at his height
Unlock the left hip, which he identifies as his central problem — 'everything comes from hips'
Straighten the curved lower back and fix the disc compression
Run again for the first time since the knee injury — 'Maybe not like competitive running, but at least...'
Be the 'too cool' version of himself again — the person he remembers being
Do it for his family as well as himself, and be able to play with his daughters
Train at home rather than in a gym, in any weather — 'I don't care if it's raining, I don't care if it's sun... Just go out and do'
Stop the pattern of quitting after holidays and busy periods

pains.text: Untreated elevated blood pressure for two years
Disc compression and curved lower back, diagnosed three years ago
Unstable right knee, untreated for a decade, which has altered his gait and caused compensations elsewhere
Locked left hip with almost no mobility — the thing he expects to be hardest
A pattern of quitting he can name precisely — 'it's not like giving up. It's like finding ways to give up'
Falls off completely after travel — two weeks in Greece last year ended his gym habit entirely
Bread and carbohydrate reliance that he links to feeling anxious and irritable
Fears he is on a downward trajectory and getting weaker
Distrust of high-pressure selling that the call itself then triggered

objections.raw_quote: You know, to be honest, 9K is not a small amount, even if we know we have good salaries here in Denmark. But either how, 9K is a lot of money, to be honest.
objections.rep_response: Isolated it properly first — 'before we talk about numbers and money, do you actually feel that you can get to your goals with Trevor... Is there anything else apart from money that could be stopping you?' — then offered the six-month tier and instalment structures.

objections.raw_quote: it might be, sounds stupid. The cheaper version, but let's see what other alternatives we have to this.
objections.rep_response: Answered with internal alternatives only — the six-month tier at $6,000, a top-up second six months at $3,000, and split payments. Never addressed the external alternative the prospect had just raised.

objections.raw_quote: Either I choose you, and I go with you for a certain amount, even if I find another chance or somebody else, it's like a way, in a way or another, I will do it. Either with you, either with somebody else.
objections.rep_response: Acknowledged it — 'That's okay. That's, that's fair enough' — and moved to presenting payment options.

objections.raw_quote: Before I released money from my account... I need to check some things about you and Trevor. I will not pay before. I don't do that. So it's like, you know, I have to be certain about some things.
objections.rep_response: Asked what he needed, then reframed the request as fear — 'isn't that fear creeping in?' — and asked 'are you looking for a reason to not to do it'. Agreed to send company information, then asked for a $100 refundable deposit to hold it overnight, which the prospect refused.

objections.raw_quote: it's like, it's a red flag for me... I know the salespeople, you know, I'm also a sales guy, but here in Denmark, we don't do it in this way. We are, we give people time... Most salespeople, that's why they it up, because they want to do it right now, now, now, now.
objections.rep_response: Tested the size threshold — 'If I would ask you for $1,000, would that be a difference?' — then pointed back at the prospect's own commitment statement. Ultimately dropped the deposit and booked the next meeting.

tiers.note: Off-menu renewal price — a second six months after completing the first, quoted as a top-up rather than a further $6,000

offer.payment_plan_terms: Against the $6,000 six-month programme: two-pay of $3,000 now and $3,000 in 30 days; or 'three or six pay, but that's gonna have like an additional interest on that' — three payments of $2,300, or six payments of $1,200. Those total $6,900 and $7,200 respectively. No interest rate, lender, or total-payable figure was stated. A $100 refundable deposit was then requested to hold the agreement overnight and refused.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Only on the deposit: 'If you tomorrow, if for some reason tomorrow you will say, look, Andy, I don't want to go with you... Fine. We're going to refund it to you.' No programme guarantee was mentioned.

prospect_financials.note: No financial picture was taken. The only disclosure was regional — 'we have good salaries here in Denmark and we have a good lifestyle' — alongside 'a pretty decent amount that I need to take out from my pocket'.

evidence: A verbal agreement was reached and explicitly ritualised: 'You want to shake hands on this?' / 'Let's shake hands on this, because I think it's more easier for everybody'
Tier and structure were chosen: 'Let's take the six months. With the six K' paid in monthly instalments
The rep moved to payment — 'We're going to go through the payment, and then I'm going to onboard you and book you a call with Trevor'
Counter-evidence, and decisive: the prospect halted before payment — 'Before I released money from my account... I need to check some things about you and Trevor. I will not pay before.'
He then refused even a $100 deposit and called the request a red flag
No payment was taken and no payment link was sent, so the verbal-agreement-plus-link rule does not apply and this is not a close
Next meeting booked for the following day at 18:00, with the prospect stating 'either I say yes or no'
outcome.next_step: Rep to email company and coach background information; follow-up meeting the next day at 18:00 on the same link, at which the prospect will give a yes or no.

notable.note: Best-executed call in the batch on process — consequence frame, commitment check and all-in question all ran properly — and simultaneously the one carrying the most integrity exposure. A prospect with two years of untreated high blood pressure, a compressed disc and a knee that subluxes was moved to a handshake on six months of loaded kettlebell training across two calls and roughly 64 minutes without one question about medical clearance, and was told his 'blood pressure is normalizing' twelve months out. The instalment options quoted exceed the list price — three payments of $2,300 is $6,900 and six of $1,200 is $7,200 against a $6,000 programme — while the prospect articulated his understanding as 'I pay a month, I use a month' for 'the six K'. When he asked to run a background check on the company before paying, the rep asked whether that was 'fear creeping in' and requested a $100 deposit to hold the deal overnight, which the prospect refused and named a red flag.
